title: The Extra chair for the guest
subtitle: 服务职业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）
meta: 主题语境：服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）　|　核心词汇：extra　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 extra 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1988 the engineer wrote of ① an extra chair for the guest in the manual, and everybody in the workshop said at once that it was ② so extra that nobody in the workshop would go near it. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the engineer, who never explained anything, had done it without a word of thanks and gone home; it was the extra ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the extra chair for the guest that anybody there had ever seen, or so the manual for April 1982 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too extra to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the worker who had come to help; the extra ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the lever at the far bench, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ an extra hour of work, and said that no worker in his right mind would call it ⑥ as extra as the hour of work they had once had in the old workshop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was extra or not, and he said so.

By 1995 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the manual. What the line asked for was ⑦ something extra, and nothing besides. The worker from the next workshop called the whole plan ⑧ quite extra; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the manual kept the names of the extra ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1998, at once, she wrote of another extra chair for the guest in the same manual, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ no less extra than anybody had expected. ⑩ The extra hour of work that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 2000, was the one she could never quite name; the extra ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 额外（前置定语 an extra chair for the guest：1988 年工程师在说明书里记下的那件额外的座位）
B. adj. 额外／外加（两处加强说法：so extra that … 与 no less extra than …）
C. adj. 额外／外加（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 额外（表语 too extra to do：母亲觉得它太额外，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 外加（前置定语 an extra hour of work：叔叔把整件事称作一桩外加的一小时工）
F. adj. 外加（同级比较 as extra as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩多加的一小时工相比）
G. adj. 外加（后置定语 something extra：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 外加（受程度副词修饰 quite extra：那位工人的评价）

items.q: an extra chair for the guest
the extra chair for the guest that
The extra hour of work that

answers.why: extra 意为“额外”，1988 年工程师在说明书里记下的是“一件额外的座位”，此处作前置定语 an extra chair for the guest。
extra 意为“额外”，此处用 so extra that 结构，说它额外到车间里没人敢靠近。
extra 意为“额外”，说明书上 四月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的额外给客人加的座位，等于最高级的说法。
extra 意为“额外”，母亲认为这件东西“太额外了，谁也用不上”，too extra to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
extra 意为“外加”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩外加的一小时工”，此处作前置定语 an extra hour of work。
extra 意为“外加”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩多加的一小时工一样外加”，同级比较用 as extra as。
extra 意为“外加”，说明书上那半行字要的是“外加的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something extra。
extra 意为“外加”，邻车间来的那位工人认为这套计划“相当外加”，quite 修饰原级 extra。
extra 意为“外加”，no less extra than 表示“其外加不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之外加不亚于任何人的预料。
extra 意为“外加”，母亲 2000 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的外加一小时工”，that 从句限定到极致。

它额外到车间里没有一个人敢靠近。（so extra that …）

It was so extra that nobody in the workshop would go near it.
